links_touching_record.rationale: The existing link FB2-LNK-SAF-000013 already records that FB2-SW-IMP-000003 is the code location carrying FB2-SW-DSN-000003. This link records the second design endpoint the same implementation realises: FB2-SW-DSN-000006, the detailed design of the same contactor element, whose internal units are CONT_OpenContactor, CONT_CloseContactor, CONT_GetFeedbackOfAllContactors, CONT_CheckFeedback and CONT_InitializationCheckOfContactorRegistry. The implementation record's own source_refs already name FB2-SRC-COD-000008, which pins CONT_CheckFeedback to lines 125-163 of contactor.c at the pinned commit, so the detailed design and the implementation share the same anchor. Direction is implementation -> design per master prompt section 13, matching FB2-LNK-SAF-000013.

FB2-SW-DSN-000006 refines FB2-SW-DSN-000003: the source side is the lower-level detailed specification and the target side is the parent architecture record. DSN-000003 allocates the contactor element and states its command and feedback interfaces at architecture level; DSN-000006 specifies the internals - the registry data model, the four-way feedback source dispatch, the linear lookup and its STD_NOT_OK contract, the precharge gate, the unconditional open-all safe-state sweep, and the TODO recording that contactor-type uniqueness per string is not checked. As with the SOA element, DSN-000003 carries design_level=detailed_design while its own standards_mappings name SWE.2 with the rationale "Software architectural design"; DSN-000006 is the record that carries the clause 8.4 content and the SWE.3 reference, and DSN-000003 is not edited by this change so its nine recorded review digests stay valid.

The power-path switch interface refines the contactor detailed-design record. That record already names SPS_RequestContactorState, SPS_GetChannelPexFeedback and SPS_GetChannelCurrentFeedback as the contactor driver's outbound calls, and it is a named symbol list rather than an interface specification. This link records the relationship so the design record is not read as having specified the boundary: it names the calls and this record gives their signatures, ranges, error paths and the two interface-level gaps the design record does not carry. The direction is specification refines design, because the specification is the finer statement.

The specification records that the contactor detailed design is verified by nothing executed. test_contactor.c is a build failure in the recorded run, so none of its 7 cases has a result, and its 2 assertions are argument-validation only against a design that decomposes into three internal units.

record_verbatim.budget_basis: cpu_time_ms is the 10 ms period imposed by the caller through BMS_Trigger, not a measured execution time, and the source states no execution figure for this module. memory_bytes and stack_bytes are zero because the module allocates nothing: the registry is a file-scope array and the only locals are a loop index, a result variable, an event variable and two channel identifiers. The registry's own size is BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS entries of CONT_CONTACTOR_STATE_s, which is a configuration-derived size this record does not express as a byte budget because the source states no element size and the packed layout is compiler-dependent. Both figures are reads of the source, not measurements.
constraints: Evaluation period: CONT_CheckFeedback is called from BMS_Trigger on every pass, and BMS_Trigger runs at the end of FTSK_RunUserCodeCyclic10ms, so commanded and sampled states are compared at 10 ms in the pinned configuration (src/app/application/bms/bms.c:918 and src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c:258-282).

Registry size: BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS is defined as 2 * BS_NR_OF_STRINGS plus BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS_OUTSIDE_STRINGS, which is 1 in the pinned configuration, giving 3 entries for a single-string system. Every loop in the module is bounded by this macro and every array indexed by the loop variable is declared with it (src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h:232 and 237).

Channel bound: the registry validator asserts spsChannel < SPS_NR_OF_AVAILABLE_SPS_CHANNELS, which is the product of the per-IC contactor channel count and the IC count. The same quantity is the size of the peripheral driver's channel arrays, so the assertion is an index bound as well as a configuration check (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:115, src/app/driver/config/sps_cfg.h:102).

Channel reservation: SPS_NR_OF_REQUIRED_CONTACTOR_CHANNELS is set to BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS, so the peripheral driver reserves exactly as many channels as the registry needs. The assertion and the reservation agree by construction at the pinned values, and both derive from the same macro (src/app/driver/config/sps_cfg.h:99).

Lookup complexity: every command and every state query is a linear scan over the registry with an early break, so cost is proportional to BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS. With 3 entries this is immaterial; the design has no index structure and would degrade linearly with string count.

Command ordering: currentSet is written before SPS_RequestContactorState is called on both the open and the close path. The registry therefore never claims a commanded state that has not been requested of the peripheral.
Feedback freshness: CONT_CheckFeedback samples every contactor on every pass and immediately compares, so the compared feedback is at most one pass old and there is no separate staleness flag.

Contactor-type uniqueness is not enforced: both CONT_InitializationCheckOfContactorRegistry and CONT_CheckFeedback carry a TODO to add a check that only one contactor of each type is configured per string, so the first-match break in the lookup is currently guaranteed by the registry contents rather than by a check.

Feedback-source fallback: the feedback dispatch tests three of the four CONT_FEEDBACK_TYPE_e values and treats the remaining else as the normally-closed case, so an unrecognised or corrupted feedback kind reads as normally closed rather than being rejected.
No latching: a feedback mismatch is re-evaluated from scratch on every pass and the module holds no counter, so a transient mismatch clears on the next agreeing pass.

alternatives: Sample feedback on demand by the consumer
Resample every contactor on every pass into the registry
decisions.rationale: Read from the source structure: CONT_CheckFeedback calls the sampler first and then compares, and CONT_GetContactorState returns the stored value rather than reading the peripheral. The design consequence, which the source does not state, is that a query can never block on the peripheral and that the registry is the single point at which feedback is observed.
decisions.selected: Resample every contactor on every pass, store into the registry, and let CONT_GetContactorState serve queries

alternatives: Report a missing feedback source as an error
Substitute the commanded state and report healthy
decisions.rationale: The source comment on CONT_GetFeedbackOfAllContactors states that if CONT_HAS_NO_FEEDBACK is configured it is assumed that the contactor has reached the requested state. Stating the assumption in the comment rather than only in the code is what makes the consequence auditable, and the consequence is that no welded-contactor detection exists for such a contactor.
decisions.selected: Substitute the commanded state, with the source comment stating the assumption explicitly

alternatives: Issue the bulk open request only for contactors currently commanded closed
Issue it for every registry entry regardless of current state
decisions.rationale: The source comment on both bulk functions states the reason: set off a request to open all contactors regardless of their current state as we want to reach a safe state. This is the one place in the module where the design rationale is recorded in the source rather than merely implemented, and it also means a contactor whose commanded state is stale is still re-commanded.

alternatives: Signal an unmatched request through a diagnosis entry as well as the return value
Return STD_NOT_OK and leave the diagnosis channel to the feedback path only
decisions.rationale: Read from the source: the command functions contain no DIAG call at all, whereas the feedback function's only DIAG call reports commanded-versus-sampled agreement. The design consequence, which the source does not state, is that a request for a contactor that was never configured is invisible to the diagnosis subsystem and exists only in the caller's return value.
decisions.selected: Return STD_NOT_OK only; no diagnosis entry for an unmatched command

declared_gaps.searched: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c at 308028fb for the two TODO comments and for any type-uniqueness comparison
declared_gaps.statement: The source does not enforce that only one contactor of each type is configured per string. Both the registry validator and the feedback evaluator carry a TODO comment naming exactly this missing check. This record therefore does not assert the invariant; it records that the first-match break in the lookup depends on an invariant the source states it does not yet check, and that a configuration violating it would make CONT_OpenContactor, CONT_CloseContactor and CONT_GetContactorState silently address the first matching entry.

declared_gaps.searched: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c at 308028fb for any counter, timer or previous-value state; the module holds no static state other than the registry
declared_gaps.statement: The source applies no debounce, no confirmation count and no latch to the feedback comparison. A single disagreeing pass raises the entry and a single agreeing pass clears it, so the persistence behaviour is a property of the diagnosis subsystem's configuration, not of this element. This record does not assert a confirmation count.
declared_gaps.topic: Contactor feedback debounce or confirmation count

declared_gaps.searched: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c at 308028fb for any read of breakingDirection; the field appears only in the registry initialiser
declared_gaps.statement: The registry carries a breakingDirection field naming the preferred opening direction for each contactor, and the source defines CONT_CHARGING_DIRECTION, CONT_DISCHARGING_DIRECTION and CONT_BIDIRECTIONAL for it. Nothing in this module reads that field. Whether opening both string contactors simultaneously is prevented, and how the preferred breaking direction is honoured, is determined by the BMS state machine and the peripheral driver, neither of which is traced here, so this record does not assert an interlock.
declared_gaps.topic: Break-before-make or interlocking between the two string contactors

declared_gaps.searched: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c at 308028fb for any settling, grace or timestamp field
declared_gaps.statement: The source does not state a settling time between SPS_RequestContactorState and the first feedback comparison, and CONT_CheckFeedback does not skip a contactor that was commanded recently. On the pass in which a command is issued the comparison may therefore be made against feedback from before the actuation completed. Whether that produces a transient diagnosis entry depends on the peripheral driver's behaviour and on how quickly the caller issues commands relative to the 10 ms period, neither of which is determined by this module.
declared_gaps.topic: Timing of the feedback relative to the command

declared_gaps.searched: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c at 308028fb for any current or voltage input
declared_gaps.statement: The source states a maximum break current in the system configuration, BS_MAIN_CONTACTORS_MAXIMUM_BREAK_CURRENT_mA, and a main fuse trigger duration, but this module reads neither and holds no current measurement. Where the breaking capability is enforced is not determined by this element and is not asserted here.
declared_gaps.topic: Physical current and voltage limits on actuation

declared_gaps.searched: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c at 308028fb for any use of a return value from SPS_RequestContactorState
declared_gaps.statement: SPS_RequestContactorState returns nothing to this module; its result is not checked and cannot be, because the module discards it. Whether the peripheral accepted the request is therefore not observable in this element, and a failed request would present only as a subsequent feedback mismatch.

declared_gaps.statement: The source states no execution-time figure and no footprint figure. The cpu_time_ms of 10 in this record is the caller's period, and the zero memory_bytes and stack_bytes follow from the module allocating nothing and holding only the registry, which is configuration-sized. Neither figure is a measurement.

decomposition.unit_role: The registry instance and its compile-time initialiser. Sized by BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS and populated with the per-contactor type, string index, feedback source kind and switch channel; the fields currentSet and feedback are written by the driver at runtime, so the initialiser supplies only the static half of each entry.

Feedback acquisition. A four-way dispatch on feedbackPinType that ends in a fall-through treated as the normally-closed case, so an unrecognised feedback kind reads as normally closed rather than being rejected.
Feedback evaluation. Samples first, then compares commanded against sampled for every contactor, and selects the diagnosis identifier by contactor type in a switch whose default arm traps.

Command path. Two structurally identical functions differing only in the state written and the switch channel requested; both scan the registry linearly for a string and type match, set currentSet first and then request the channel, and return STD_NOT_OK when no entry matched.

Precharge gating layer. Each consults the per-string precharge configuration and delegates to CONT_CloseContactor or CONT_OpenContactor only when the string has one, otherwise returning STD_NOT_OK without touching the registry.

Bulk command paths. Both iterate the whole registry without a lookup and without consulting the current state; the first requests every channel off, the second only the entries whose type is CONT_PRECHARGE. Both carry the source comment that the request is issued regardless of current state because the intent is to reach a safe state.

Feedback query. The same linear lookup as the command path, returning the sampled feedback rather than the commanded state, and initialising its result to CONT_SWITCH_UNDEFINED so an unmatched query is distinguishable from a matched one that reports off.

Registry validator. Two assertions per contactor: the configured channel must be within the available channel count, and the channel must report contactor affiliation. Its body also carries a TODO recording that the uniqueness of contactor type per string is not checked.

Switch-peripheral driver boundary. Every physical actuation and every feedback read leaves this module here; the module holds no register knowledge of its own beyond the channel number it was configured with.

derived_findings.evidence: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:90-92 for the substitution and 131-133 for the comparison that consumes it, against the configuration at src/app/driver/config/contactor_cfg.c:84-90
derived_findings.finding: A contactor configured CONT_HAS_NO_FEEDBACK is reported healthy unconditionally. The acquisition path assigns feedback from currentSet on that arm, so the comparison in CONT_CheckFeedback is a tautology and the diagnosis entry is cleared on every pass. This is a property of the configuration, and it means the welded-contactor detection the feedback path otherwise provides does not exist for that entry.

The feedback dispatch has no explicit normally-closed arm. Three of the four CONT_FEEDBACK_TYPE_e values are tested by name and the final else is commented as the normally-closed case, so a corrupted or out-of-range feedback kind is read with the normally-closed sense instead of being rejected.

derived_findings.evidence: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:112 and 130 for the TODO comments, and 169-178 for the first-match break in CONT_OpenContactor
derived_findings.finding: The lookup break and the missing uniqueness check are the same issue seen from two sides. CONT_OpenContactor, CONT_CloseContactor and CONT_GetContactorState all break on the first string-and-type match, and the source records in two separate TODO comments that the uniqueness of contactor type per string is not checked. A configuration with two matching entries would therefore address only the first, silently.

derived_findings.evidence: src/app/driver/config/contactor_cfg.h:114 for the field and 100-104 for the enumerators, against src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c which contains no read of breakingDirection
derived_findings.finding: breakingDirection is configured but never read by this module. The field is declared in the registry structure and populated in the initialiser, and the three enumerator values exist, but no function in the module reads it, so the preferred opening direction is carried as data with no consumer inside the element.

derived_findings.evidence: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:203-221 for the gate returning STD_NOT_OK on the negative precharge case, against 165-182 for a genuine lookup miss
derived_findings.finding: STD_NOT_OK from the command path carries two distinct meanings. CONT_ClosePrecharge and CONT_OpenPrecharge return STD_NOT_OK both when the string has no precharge contactor, which is a normal configuration outcome, and when the delegated lookup missed, which is not. A caller cannot distinguish the two from the return value.

record_verbatim.design_scope_note: FB2-SW-DSN-000003 records the contactor element at architecture level. As with the SOA element, that record carries design_level=detailed_design while its standards_mappings name SWE.2 and its rationale reads "Software architectural design"; this record is the one that carries the clause 8.4 content and the SWE.3 reference. The link FB2-SW-DSN-000006 refines FB2-SW-DSN-000003 records the relationship in the registry.

failure_response.failure_mode: Configured switch channel does not exist
failure_response.reaction: The assertion traps during CONT_Initialize. There is no diagnosis entry and no degraded start; the system does not proceed to operate contactors with an invalid registry.
failure_response.recovery: None in the source; the remedy is to correct the configuration and re-initialise.

failure_response.detection: FAS_ASSERT(SPS_AFF_CONTACTOR == channelAffiliation), which queries the peripheral driver rather than trusting the configuration
failure_response.failure_mode: Configured channel exists but is affiliated to something other than a contactor
failure_response.reaction: The assertion traps. This check is what catches two contactor entries sharing one channel, because the first entry written would leave the channel correctly affiliated but a mis-numbered second entry would not.

failure_response.detection: The default arm of the type switch in CONT_CheckFeedback
failure_response.failure_mode: Contactor registry holds a type outside plus, minus and precharge
failure_response.reaction: FAS_ASSERT(FAS_TRAP) executes and the pass stops. The module treats an unconfigured type as unrecoverable rather than skipping it, which is a deliberate fail-stop on a configuration defect.
failure_response.recovery: None in the source; a trap is terminal for the caller.

failure_response.detection: The linear scan completes without a match; the function's own control flow detects it
failure_response.failure_mode: Command issued for a string and type the registry does not contain
failure_response.reaction: STD_NOT_OK is returned, no registry field is written and no peripheral request is issued. The failure is silent at the hardware level and does not raise a diagnosis entry.
failure_response.recovery: None in the source. A caller that ignores the return value has no indication that nothing happened.

failure_response.detection: CONT_CheckFeedback compares currentSet against the sampled feedback each pass and finds them unequal
failure_response.failure_mode: Contactor does not reach the commanded state, for example welded or mechanically stuck
failure_response.reaction: The diagnosis entry for that contactor type is raised with DIAG_EVENT_NOT_OK at DIAG_STRING impact. The module does not retry, does not latch and does not escalate; the reaction belongs to the diagnosis subsystem and the BMS state machine.
failure_response.recovery: Clears automatically on the first pass where the two agree, because the module keeps no counter and re-evaluates from current state every pass.

failure_response.detection: Not a failure: the CONT_HAS_NO_FEEDBACK configuration is handled by substituting the commanded state
failure_response.failure_mode: A contactor has no feedback source configured
failure_response.reaction: The comparison is satisfied by construction and the diagnosis entry is always cleared. Such a contactor is permanently reported as healthy.
failure_response.recovery: None available, and none needed in the module's own terms. Recorded because the feedback-mismatch reaction above does not apply to this configuration, so a system relying on feedback for a welded-contactor detection must not rely on it for a contactor configured CONT_HAS_NO_FEEDBACK.

failure_response.detection: The BMS state machine reaches the substate that handles supply-voltage loss
failure_response.failure_mode: Loss of the 30 V supply to the contactor electronics
failure_response.reaction: CONT_OpenAllContactors requests every registry channel off, SPS_SwitchOffAllGeneralIoChannels requests the general IO channels off, and the machine leaves through the open-strings-exit substate. This is the one bulk path in the module and it is unconditional, matching the source comment that a request is issued regardless of current state because the intent is to reach a safe state.
failure_response.recovery: Not stated in the source; re-closing the string is a BMS state-machine decision outside this element.

failure_response.failure_mode: Out-of-range string or undefined contactor type reaches a command entry point
failure_response.reaction: The assertion traps before the scan, so the STD_NOT_OK return can never carry this meaning.

interfaces.call_contract: FAS_ASSERT on both arguments traps before the scan, so the NOT_OK return can only mean no match, never a rejected argument. The scan breaks on the first match, so if the registry ever contained two entries with the same string and type the first would win silently; the source records that this cannot currently happen because the uniqueness check is a TODO.
interfaces.error_signalling: STD_RETURN_TYPE_e, returning STD_OK only when a registry entry matched both the string index and the contactor type, and STD_NOT_OK when the scan completed without a match. The failure is therefore reported for an unconfigured request. A request naming a valid string and a valid type for which the string has no such contactor is not distinguished from a request naming a type the string does not carry.

signals.name: stringNumber
signals.range: asserted stringNumber < BS_NR_OF_STRINGS; the source states no numeric bound, it asserts against the named macro
signals.source_value_basis: named configuration macro BS_NR_OF_STRINGS, asserted rather than compared against a literal
signals.validity: FAS_ASSERT(stringNumber < BS_NR_OF_STRINGS) on both the open and the close path. An out-of-range string traps; it is not reported through the return value.

signals.name: contactor
signals.range: CONT_PLUS, CONT_MINUS or CONT_PRECHARGE accepted; CONT_UNDEFINED rejected
signals.source_value_basis: named design-time enumerator CONT_UNDEFINED, asserted as a forbidden value
signals.validity: FAS_ASSERT(contactor != CONT_UNDEFINED). Note the asymmetry: the type argument is checked against a forbidden value, not against a bound, so a value outside the enumeration entirely is not caught here - it simply fails the registry match and yields STD_NOT_OK.

signals.name: currentSet
signals.range: CONT_SWITCH_OFF on the open path, CONT_SWITCH_ON on the close path
signals.validity: Written before the channel request is issued, so the registry always holds the intent before the hardware is asked to follow it. This ordering is the reason CONT_CheckFeedback can compare intent against feedback without a separate request-pending flag.

interfaces.call_contract: FAS_ASSERT(stringNumber < BS_NR_OF_STRINGS) traps on an out-of-range string. The precharge check is a gate, not a validation: it changes which function is called, and its negative case is indistinguishable at the return value from a genuine miss.
interfaces.error_signalling: STD_RETURN_TYPE_e, forwarding the result of the delegated CONT_CloseContactor or CONT_OpenContactor when the string has a precharge contactor, and returning STD_NOT_OK without calling the registry when it does not. The same STD_NOT_OK therefore covers both a string with no precharge contactor and a genuine lookup miss.

signals.name: bs_stringsWithPrecharge
signals.range: compared against BS_STRING_WITH_PRECHARGE; a string without a precharge contactor takes a different value
signals.source_value_basis: named configuration constant BS_STRING_WITH_PRECHARGE compared by equality against a configured per-string value
signals.validity: FAS_ASSERT(stringNumber < BS_NR_OF_STRINGS) before the array is indexed, so the index is bounded. The element type and its full value set are not declared in this module and are not asserted here.

interfaces.call_contract: The loop runs over all BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS entries every pass, so every contactor is resampled regardless of whether anything changed. The function carries no precondition of its own and no assertion.
interfaces.error_signalling: No error return; the function is void and returns the sampled value by writing the registry. A peripheral read failure is not representable in the return type and is not checked here.

signals.name: feedbackPinType
signals.source_value_basis: closed enumeration in src/app/driver/config/contactor_cfg.h:77-82, dispatched by literal equality
signals.validity: Dispatched by a chain of equality tests. CONT_HAS_NO_FEEDBACK substitutes the commanded state for the feedback; CONT_FEEDBACK_THROUGH_CURRENT reads the channel's current feedback; CONT_FEEDBACK_NORMALLY_OPEN reads the port-expander line with the normally-open sense; and the final else reads it with the opposite sense. There is no fourth explicit test, so any value outside the enumeration is handled as normally closed.

signals.name: feedback
signals.range: CONT_SWITCH_OFF or CONT_SWITCH_ON as returned by the peripheral driver; CONT_SWITCH_UNDEFINED is never written by the acquisition path
signals.source_value_basis: the substitution `feedback = currentSet` is a literal assignment on the CONT_HAS_NO_FEEDBACK arm
signals.validity: For a contactor configured CONT_HAS_NO_FEEDBACK the acquired value is a copy of currentSet, so feedback agrees with the command by construction and CONT_CheckFeedback always clears the diagnosis entry for that contactor. Such a contactor cannot report a stuck or welded state.

interfaces.call_contract: The default arm of the switch executes FAS_ASSERT(FAS_TRAP) when the registry holds a type other than plus, minus or precharge, so an unconfigured type stops the pass rather than being skipped.
interfaces.error_signalling: No error return. The diagnosis subsystem's return value is not captured, so a refused entry is indistinguishable here from an accepted one. The only failure signalling this module performs itself is the trap in the switch default arm.

signals.name: feedbackStatus
signals.range: DIAG_EVENT_OK when currentSet equals feedback, DIAG_EVENT_NOT_OK otherwise
signals.validity: Initialised to DIAG_EVENT_NOT_OK before the comparison, so a contactor whose type is not one of the three handled values would be reported as not ok were it not for the trap in the default arm.

signals.name: diagnosis identifier by contactor type
signals.source_value_basis: literal constants at the three switch arms in src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c
signals.validity: Selected by a switch on the registry's type field at DIAG_STRING impact carrying the contactor's own stringIndex rather than the loop index, which matters because the registry is not ordered by string.

interfaces.call_contract: No precondition and no assertion. The caller in this codebase is the BMS state machine's supply-voltage-loss substate, which invokes the sweep and then the general-IO sweep before leaving through the open-strings-exit substate.
interfaces.error_signalling: No error return; both sweeps are void and issue no diagnosis entry. A request that the peripheral driver could not honour produces no indication in this module.

signals.name: SPS_CHANNEL_OFF
signals.range: one request per registry entry; CONT_OpenAllContactors issues BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS of them
signals.source_value_basis: the loop bound is BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS and the request literal is SPS_CHANNEL_OFF
signals.validity: Issued unconditionally, without reading currentSet. A contactor already open is therefore re-commanded open on every sweep.

record_verbatim.provenance_note: Every path, symbol and line range in this record was checked against the tree at commit 308028fb with git show, not against the working tree. The CONT_CheckFeedback citation was cross-checked against source anchor FB2-SRC-COD-000008, which pins that function to lines 125-163 of src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c at that commit. The registry initialiser at src/app/driver/config/contactor_cfg.c:67 is cited as the definition site of cont_contactorStates in that translation unit; the declaration at src/app/driver/config/contactor_cfg.h:121 is cited separately. This record does not assert ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool qualification, an ASPICE capability level or human approval; human_approval_status is pending, production_authorized is false and product_verification_credit is false.
responsibilities: Hold the contactor registry: one entry per contactor carrying the commanded state, the last observed feedback, the feedback source kind, the owning string, the contactor type, the switch-peripheral channel and the preferred breaking direction (src/app/driver/config/contactor_cfg.h:107-121)

Translate a request to open or close a named contactor on a named string into a switch-peripheral channel request, and report whether the registry contained a matching entry (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:165-201)

Sample the auxiliary feedback of every contactor from whichever of the four configured feedback sources that contactor uses, and publish it into the registry (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:86-106)
Compare commanded state against sampled feedback per contactor and raise or clear one diagnosis entry per contactor type (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:125-163)
Gate the precharge-specific open and close calls on the string actually having a precharge contactor configured (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:203-221)
Open every contactor unconditionally as a safe-state sweep, without consulting the current state (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:236-244)
Validate the registry once at initialisation: every configured channel must exist and every channel must be affiliated to a contactor (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:108-122)
